findings.name: Conv2d
findings.title: Discrete cross-correlation
findings.equation: y[c,i,j] = b[c] + Σ_k Σ_u Σ_v W[c,k,u,v] · x[k, s·i + d·u − p, s·j + d·v − p]
freedom: The same 216 weights are reused at every one of the 1,024 positions. That reuse is the whole idea: it assumes what matters is the same everywhere in the image, and it is why a convolution has so few parameters for what it does.
Dilation widens the window without adding a single parameter: d=1 already reaches 3 pixels using 3×3 weights. Stacking dilations 1,2,4,8 grows the reach exponentially with depth.

Groups divide the parameters by g. At g=C_in each filter sees one channel — that is a depthwise convolution, 27 parameters instead of 216, and a 1×1 convolution after it mixes the channels back. That factorisation is most of what makes mobile architectures small.
